bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is effectively debt-free and investment-heavy: consolidated total equity of Rs 1,313.0 Cr at Mar-26 (Rs 1,061.8 Cr at Mar-25) against finance cost of only Rs 4.3 Cr in FY26, with current investments of Rs 896.0 Cr, other non-current investments of Rs 205.0 Cr and cash & cash equivalents of Rs 91.6 Cr.
- FY26 consolidated cash flows: net cash from operating activities Rs 362.9 Cr, net cash used in investing activities Rs -370.1 Cr, and net cash used in financing activities Rs -100.0 Cr, leaving a net decrease in cash of Rs -107.2 Cr.
- Return ratios are shown declining off a high base - Return on Equity 30%, 31%, 34%, 30%, 26% and Return on Capital Employed 37%, 35%, 39%, 38%, 32% across FY22 to FY26 (deck defines ROE = PAT/Total Equity and ROCE = EBIT/(Total Debt + Total Equity)).
- Growth is positioned as low-capital-intensity: facilities are described as "ready for incremental growth without capex", with capital work in progress at nil at Mar-26 (Rs 8.5 Cr at Mar-25) and intangible assets under development of Rs 14.3 Cr.
- Gross tangible assets rise across the FY22-FY26 series from Rs 361 crore to Rs 579 crore (the extraction interleaves the year labels with the values, so individual year-to-value bindings are not asserted).

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Dependence on a limited number of large customers may affect volume stability and commercial bargaining position. The Company mitigates this by broadening its customer and product base, increasing wallet share with existing customers and developing opportunities across lightweighting, emission adjacencies and exports.
- Market concentration - predominantly domestic revenue base — A predominantly domestic revenue base increases exposure to changes in the Indian automotive cycle; exports contributed only 0.37% of total turnover in FY 2025-26. SMIL established a dedicated global business team in FY25 and continues to engage customers across North America and Europe with RFQ activity in emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields and other adjacencies.
- Regulatory and technology-transition risk — Changes, delays or revisions in emission, fuel-efficiency and powertrain regulations may affect product demand, program timing, technology requirements and investment cycles. Varying adoption rates across ICE, hybrid, CNG, flex-fuel and electric powertrains require sustained R&D and capital investment. Mitigated by benchmarking evolving regulations, engaging OEMs on future requirements, strengthening R&D and validation, and diversifying into thermal management and powertrain-agnostic lightweighting products.
- Geopolitical and supply-chain risk — Geopolitical developments, trade and tariff actions, shipping-route disruptions and volatility in raw-material, freight, insurance and currency costs may affect supply continuity, customer schedules and operating costs. Mitigated by the India-centric manufacturing footprint, backward integration, customer-aligned sourcing, localisation initiatives and a flexible operating approach.
- Commodity price risk — Commodities form a major part of raw materials for the product portfolio, making commodity price risk one of the most important market risks. Steel and allied commodities were largely stable during the year but gained volatility towards the latter part of the year on geopolitical conditions, and precious metals saw a significant rise in prices. The Company has price indexing arrangements with customers for price movements; exposure to stainless steel, aluminized coated mild steel and mild steel is disclosed as entirely unhedged (Nil across domestic OTC, domestic exchange, international OTC and international exchange).
- Human resource risk — Business performance may be affected by attrition, availability of critical skills, capability development and industrial-relations issues. Mitigated through structured recruitment, compensation, training, engagement and employee-welfare practices.
- Cyber security and technology obsolescence risk — Technology obsolescence and cyber threats such as malware, phishing and ransomware may affect information security and business continuity. The Company conducts VAPT and infrastructure security audits, addresses identified gaps and maintains data-backup and business-continuity measures.
- Legal compliance risk — As a listed company operating plants across multiple states, SMIL is subject to corporate, securities, labour, environmental and state-specific laws and regulations. Mitigated by strengthened internal compliance capabilities, external legal and specialist advice, and a portal-based compliance-monitoring platform.
- Risk of costs associated with eventualities — Events such as fire, theft, natural hazards, transit damage, employee injury, product recall, litigation and third-party claims may result in financial or operational loss. The Company maintains appropriate insurance coverage and operating policies and procedures.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SMIL operates nine manufacturing facilities across India - Chennai (2), Chakan/Pune (3), Nashik (2), Sanand (1) and Uttarakhand (1) - supported by an R&D centre at Mahindra World City, Chennai and a Design and Development Centre at Namyang, South Korea. The BRSR Section A footprint disclosure records 9 plants and 3 offices nationally plus 1 international office, with commercial operations yet to commence at one plant. During FY26 the Chakan Plant-III lightweighting facility commenced SOP with modular capacity deployment aligned to customer requirements, and the Company ramped up its Chakan suspension plant. It also initiated a new modular, scalable facility in Uttarakhand to improve proximity to customers and support future growth in both emission and lightweighting products in the Northern region, listed on the corporate timeline as 2026 - Set up plant in Uttarakhand. On the programme side, SOPs for previously announced control arms and links programs commenced as scheduled and the CEV temperature-controlled tube programme entered SOP and began ramping up, following the SOP of temperature-controlled tubes for one of the largest off-highway manufacturers in India. R&D facilities were augmented during FY26 to support control arms and links development. The lightweighting portfolio is being extended into subframes and torsion beams under the October 2025 Technology Licensing Agreement with Donghee Industrial Company Limited of South Korea, with FY26 focused on technology transfer, localisation, capability building and customer engagement. Backward-integration assets comprise centralised ERW tube manufacturing at SMIL-MWC with two facilities of diverse diametrical capability, three stamping plants with 50+ stamping machines across Chennai, Nashik and Sanand, and welding and testing infrastructure; the Company describes these facilities as fully backward integrated and ready for incremental growth without capex. FY27 capex is directed towards R&D augmentation, readiness for new emission norms, and supporting new program SOPs. On M&A the approach is described as disciplined but active, evaluating powertrain-agnostic products and lightweighting technologies against strategic fit, customer relevance, technology access, export potential and ROCE discipline.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Evolving regulation is a long-term growth driver: WLTP and future BS7 norms are expected to increase focus on catalyst efficiency, calibration, thermal management and system durability, increasing content per engine and driving market consolidation on technology requirements
- BS6.3 incorporating WLTP has been notified for implementation from 1 April 2027 for vehicles below 3.5 tonne GVW, increasing technology content across the value chain
- The proposed CAFE III framework for M1 passenger vehicles reinforces a multi-technology approach - EVs, hybrids, CNG, flex-fuel, powertrain-efficiency measures and lightweighting - and, except for pure EVs, these pathways continue to support the relevance of engineered emission systems while lightweighting remains applicable across all powertrains
- The tractor-emission roadmap is moving towards power-category-specific norms and timelines, with the near-term opportunity expected to be concentrated in mufflers and integrated mufflers
- Increasing OEM focus on fuel efficiency, CO2 reduction, EV range, safety and platform optimisation continues to support demand for lightweight structural products; a 10% weight reduction can improve EV range by 13.7%
- Global supply-chain diversification and localisation by customers in Europe and the United States strengthens India's relevance as a manufacturing base, creating an export opportunity for emission systems, thermal-management components, lightweighting products, temperature-controlled tubes and heat shields
- The India-US and India-EU trade deals announced during the year are described as structural tailwinds that improve long-term sourcing confidence among global OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers
- The core emission business contributed 88% of revenues across PV and CV segments in FY26 and remains the foundation of financial performance; the lightweighting vertical now constitutes approximately 10% of gross sales
- Indian automotive component industry turnover reached Rs 7.6 lakh crore in FY26, growing 12.7% year-on-year, with passenger vehicles the largest end-user segment at 45% of component supplies to OEMs
- India remains a multi-powertrain market - EV penetration was 4.3% in passenger vehicles in FY26, with CNG/LPG at 22% and hybrids at 8.2% of PV retail volumes - supporting continued relevance of engineered emission systems
- India-centric manufacturing footprint and backward integration across tubes, stampings, fabrication and assemblies support resilience, with raw-material sourcing largely aligned with customer-managed supply chains
- Key risks to the outlook include geopolitical uncertainty, raw-material volatility, critical-material availability and logistics costs
- The order book built in FY25 and FY26 in the lightweighting vertical points to significant growth in this vertical by FY28 relative to the FY26 base
- Export orders secured during FY26 from various customers including the largest engine and genset manufacturer in North America and Top 3 global agricultural equipment manufacturers
- A strategic first pilot order received from a large US-based heavy industry emission company, giving entry into another US CV OEM
- RFQ activity underway across emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields and other adjacencies with customers in North America and Europe
- SOPs for previously announced control arms and links programs commenced as scheduled during FY26, and the CEV temperature-controlled tube program entered SOP and began ramping up
- Portfolio diversification and a stronger order book are cited by the MD as the levers being converted into sustainable long-term value

risks.note: Changes, delays or revisions in emission, fuel-efficiency and powertrain regulations may affect product demand, program timing, technology requirements and investment cycles. Varying adoption rates across ICE, hybrid, CNG, flex-fuel and electric powertrains require sustained R&D and capital investment. Mitigated by benchmarking evolving regulations, engaging OEMs on future requirements, strengthening R&D and validation, and diversifying into thermal management and powertrain-agnostic lightweighting products.

Geopolitical developments, trade and tariff actions, shipping-route disruptions and volatility in raw-material, freight, insurance and currency costs may affect supply continuity, customer schedules and operating costs. Mitigated by the India-centric manufacturing footprint, backward integration, customer-aligned sourcing, localisation initiatives and a flexible operating approach.

Commodities form a major part of raw materials for the product portfolio, making commodity price risk one of the most important market risks. Steel and allied commodities were largely stable during the year but gained volatility towards the latter part of the year on geopolitical conditions, and precious metals saw a significant rise in prices. The Company has price indexing arrangements with customers for price movements; exposure to stainless steel, aluminized coated mild steel and mild steel is disclosed as entirely unhedged (Nil across domestic OTC, domestic exchange, international OTC and international exchange).

Business performance may be affected by attrition, availability of critical skills, capability development and industrial-relations issues. Mitigated through structured recruitment, compensation, training, engagement and employee-welfare practices.

Technology obsolescence and cyber threats such as malware, phishing and ransomware may affect information security and business continuity. The Company conducts VAPT and infrastructure security audits, addresses identified gaps and maintains data-backup and business-continuity measures.

currentContext.expansion: SMIL operates nine manufacturing facilities across India - Chennai (2), Chakan/Pune (3), Nashik (2), Sanand (1) and Uttarakhand (1) - supported by an R&D centre at Mahindra World City, Chennai and a Design and Development Centre at Namyang, South Korea. The BRSR Section A footprint disclosure records 9 plants and 3 offices nationally plus 1 international office, with commercial operations yet to commence at one plant. During FY26 the Chakan Plant-III lightweighting facility commenced SOP with modular capacity deployment aligned to customer requirements, and the Company ramped up its Chakan suspension plant. It also initiated a new modular, scalable facility in Uttarakhand to improve proximity to customers and support future growth in both emission and lightweighting products in the Northern region, listed on the corporate timeline as 2026 - Set up plant in Uttarakhand. On the programme side, SOPs for previously announced control arms and links programs commenced as scheduled and the CEV temperature-controlled tube programme entered SOP and began ramping up, following the SOP of temperature-controlled tubes for one of the largest off-highway manufacturers in India. R&D facilities were augmented during FY26 to support control arms and links development. The lightweighting portfolio is being extended into subframes and torsion beams under the October 2025 Technology Licensing Agreement with Donghee Industrial Company Limited of South Korea, with FY26 focused on technology transfer, localisation, capability building and customer engagement. FY27 capex is directed towards R&D augmentation, readiness for new emission norms, and supporting new program SOPs. one-line thesis: Sharda Motor delivered robust Q4FY26 revenue growth (+30% YoY) driven by volume recovery and new lightweighting SOPs, with FY27 poised for acceleration via CAFE III-induced content per vehicle increases and high-margin export ramp-ups. Margins held steady at 11.6% despite catalyst cost volatility, while the order book expands into subframes and global agri-equipment segments.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 971.8cr (Q4, +30% YoY), INR 3,396.8cr (FY26, +20% YoY); EBITDA: INR 112.9cr (Q4, +12% YoY), Margin 11.6%; PAT: INR 89.4cr (Q4), INR 345.4cr (FY26, +9.7% YoY); One-offs: INR 22.41cr gain on land sale (Q1), INR 4.26cr loss on new Labour codes (Q3/Q4); Order Book: Robust pipeline in lightweighting (targeting 3x FY26 levels by FY28) and new export wins ($12mn lifetime value announced); Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified in transcript, balance sheet described as strong for M&A.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Acceleration expected in FY27/FY28 from lightweighting SOPs and exports; Margin: Stable to improving as lightweighting scales (currently ~9% of sales, targeting significant increase); Order Inflow: Healthy RFQ pipeline in Europe/US; Capex: INR 90-110cr for FY27 (excl. new facility capex linked to specific customer orders).
order book & pipeline: Lightweighting market share rose to 14% (from 12.5%); New export order from global agri-OEM ($2mn annual, $10mn lifetime, SOP Q1 FY28); US heavy industry emission test order; North American engine/genset SOP delayed to Q3 FY27; Donghee TLA enabling subframe/torsion beam content addition.
segment / subsidiary detail: Emission (PV 43%, CV 44%); Lightweighting/Suspension (9% of sales, high growth trajectory); Off-highway/Exports/Gensets (1% currently, rapid growth phase); Catalyst costs impacted reported value mix but value-added sales in lightweighting grew.
growth verticals / optionality: CAFE III norms (April 2027) driving content per vehicle up by INR 4,000-10,000 via lightweighting; BS7 readiness; China Plus One sourcing wins in Europe/US; Potential M&A in tech-fit areas; TREM5 niche opportunities in integrated mufflers.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 11.6% (Q4); Lightweighting margins described as 'decent' and improving with scale; Export margins gross higher but net similar due to working capital; Catalyst price volatility impacted top-line mix but gross profit grew 13% in Q4.
capex / expansion: FY27 guidance INR 90-110cr for R&D augmentation and new program SOPs; Additional capex for new facilities (e.g., Uttarakhand, Chakan 3) is modular and customer-order linked.
capital allocation: Disciplined M&A approach with strong balance sheet flexibility; Focus on ROCE and strategic fit (tech/customer); Organic capex linked to order visibility.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension (West Asia) affecting crude/commodity prices and shipping; Regulatory delays (TREM5 design finalization); Customer concentration (exclusion of largest PV OEM); Inventory buildup (though days improved).
management quality / tone: Confident on structural growth drivers (CAFE III, Lightweighting); Prudent on capex and M&A valuations; Transparent on delays (OEM-driven); Optimistic on export diversification.
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory spike to INR 75cr is purely scale-driven (days improved); TREM5 opportunity now niche (mufflers only for 19-37kW segment) but R&D spend aids export wins; Catalyst cost inflation masks true lightweighting volume growth in revenue % terms.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Acceleration expected in FY27/FY28 from lightweighting SOPs and exports; Margin: Stable to improving as lightweighting scales (currently ~9% of sales, targeting significant increase); Order Inflow: Healthy RFQ pipeline in Europe/US; Capex: INR 90-110cr for FY27 (excl. new facility capex linked to specific customer orders).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: CAFE III norms (April 2027) driving content per vehicle up by INR 4,000-10,000 via lightweighting; BS7 readiness; China Plus One sourcing wins in Europe/US; Potential M&A in tech-fit areas; TREM5 niche opportunities in integrated mufflers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Evolving regulation is a long-term growth driver: WLTP and future BS7 norms are expected to increase focus on catalyst efficiency, calibration, thermal management and system durability, increasing content per engine and driving market consolidation on technology requirements
- BS6.3 incorporating WLTP has been notified for implementation from 1 April 2027 for vehicles below 3.5 tonne GVW, increasing technology content across the value chain
- The proposed CAFE III framework for M1 passenger vehicles reinforces a multi-technology approach - EVs, hybrids, CNG, flex-fuel, powertrain-efficiency measures and lightweighting - and, except for pure EVs, these pathways continue to support the relevance of engineered emission systems while lightweighting remains applicable across all powertrains
- The tractor-emission roadmap is moving towards power-category-specific norms and timelines, with the near-term opportunity expected to be concentrated in mufflers and integrated mufflers
- Increasing OEM focus on fuel efficiency, CO2 reduction, EV range, safety and platform optimisation continues to support demand for lightweight structural products; a 10% weight reduction can improve EV range by 13.7%
- Global supply-chain diversification and localisation by customers in Europe and the United States strengthens India's relevance as a manufacturing base, creating an export opportunity for emission systems, thermal-management components, lightweighting products, temperature-controlled tubes and heat shields
- The India-US and India-EU trade deals announced during the year are described as structural tailwinds that improve long-term sourcing confidence among global OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers
- The core emission business contributed 88% of revenues across PV and CV segments in FY26 and remains the foundation of financial performance; the lightweighting vertical now constitutes approximately 10% of gross sales
- Indian automotive component industry turnover reached Rs 7.6 lakh crore in FY26, growing 12.7% year-on-year, with passenger vehicles the largest end-user segment at 45% of component supplies to OEMs
- India remains a multi-powertrain market - EV penetration was 4.3% in passenger vehicles in FY26, with CNG/LPG at 22% and hybrids at 8.2% of PV retail volumes - supporting continued relevance of engineered emission systems
- India-centric manufacturing footprint and backward integration across tubes, stampings, fabrication and assemblies support resilience, with raw-material sourcing largely aligned with customer-managed supply chains
- Key risks to the outlook include geopolitical uncertainty, raw-material volatility, critical-material availability and logistics costs
- The order book built in FY25 and FY26 in the lightweighting vertical points to significant growth in this vertical by FY28 relative to the FY26 base
- Export orders secured during FY26 from various customers including the largest engine and genset manufacturer in North America and Top 3 global agricultural equipment manufacturers
- A strategic first pilot order received from a large US-based heavy industry emission company, giving entry into another US CV OEM
- RFQ activity underway across emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, heat shields and other adjacencies with customers in North America and Europe
- SOPs for previously announced control arms and links programs commenced as scheduled during FY26, and the CEV temperature-controlled tube program entered SOP and began ramping up
- Portfolio diversification and a stronger order book are cited by the MD as the levers being converted into sustainable long-term value

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 11.6% (Q4); Lightweighting margins described as 'decent' and improving with scale; Export margins gross higher but net similar due to working capital; Catalyst price volatility impacted top-line mix but gross profit grew 13% in Q4.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Disciplined M&A approach with strong balance sheet flexibility; Focus on ROCE and strategic fit (tech/customer); Organic capex linked to order visibility.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SMIL operates nine manufacturing facilities across India - Chennai (2), Chakan/Pune (3), Nashik (2), Sanand (1) and Uttarakhand (1) - supported by an R&D centre at Mahindra World City, Chennai and a Design and Development Centre at Namyang, South Korea. The BRSR Section A footprint disclosure records 9 plants and 3 offices nationally plus 1 international office, with commercial operations yet to commence at one plant. During FY26 the Chakan Plant-III lightweighting facility commenced SOP with modular capacity deployment aligned to customer requirements, and the Company ramped up its Chakan suspension plant. It also initiated a new modular, scalable facility in Uttarakhand to improve proximity to customers and support future growth in both emission and lightweighting products in the Northern region, listed on the corporate timeline as 2026 - Set up plant in Uttarakhand. On the programme side, SOPs for previously announced control arms and links programs commenced as scheduled and the CEV temperature-controlled tube programme entered SOP and began ramping up, following the SOP of temperature-controlled tubes for one of the largest off-highway manufacturers in India. R&D facilities were augmented during FY26 to support control arms and links development. The lightweighting portfolio is being extended into subframes and torsion beams under the October 2025 Technology Licensing Agreement with Donghee Industrial Company Limited of South Korea, with FY26 focused on technology transfer, localisation, capability building and customer engagement. Backward-integration assets comprise centralised ERW tube manufacturing at SMIL-MWC with two facilities of diverse diametrical capability, three stamping plants with 50+ stamping machines across Chennai, Nashik and Sanand, and welding and testing infrastructure; the Company describes these facilities as fully backward integrated and ready for incremental growth without capex. FY27 capex is directed towards R&D augmentation, readiness for new emission norms, and supporting new program SOPs. On M&A the approach is described as disciplined but active, evaluating powertrain-agnostic products and lightweighting technologies against strategic fit, customer relevance, technology access, export potential and ROCE discipline.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on structural growth drivers (CAFE III, Lightweighting); Prudent on capex and M&A valuations; Transparent on delays (OEM-driven); Optimistic on export diversification.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Approximately 30% value market share in India for passenger vehicle and light commercial vehicle emission systems
- Approximately 14% value market share for PV and LCV control arms and links in India in FY26, up from around 12% in FY25
- Backward integration across tube mills, stampings, fabrication and assemblies - centralised ERW tube manufacturing at SMIL-MWC with two facilities of diverse diametrical capability, and 3 stamping plants with 50+ stamping machines across Chennai, Nashik and Sanand
- In-house R&D: R&D centre at Mahindra World City, Chennai (exhaust systems since 2002, emission control systems since 2010) plus a Design and Development Centre at Namyang, South Korea, with 125+ trained engineers for Design, CFD, FEA and Acoustics, IATF 16949-2016 certified
- R&D capability spanning BS6, BS6.2, TREM5, STAGE5, TIER4 and TIER5 emission norms, with end-to-end testing including hot vibration lab, flow lab, semi anechoic chamber, thermal lab, engine testing lab and prototyping shop
- Patent portfolio of 22 cumulative filings and 4 patents granted by end of FY26, with nine filings and one grant added during FY26
- Joint venture with Purem (formerly Eberspaecher) of Germany and a technology licensing agreement with Donghee Industrial Co. Ltd. of South Korea giving access to global chassis, subframe and torsion beam technology
- Manufacturing footprint located in India's key automotive clusters, giving proximity to customers and optimised logistics
- Zero-debt balance sheet with a strong surplus, giving flexibility to invest in future growth areas
- CRISIL AA-/Positive long-term and CRISIL A1+ short-term ratings reaffirmed on bank working capital facilities
- Advanced welding capabilities including DC Welding, DC Pulse Welding, CMT Welding and Micro MIG welding
- Long-standing OEM recognition including multiple Mahindra & Mahindra supplier and quality awards between 2014 and 2025

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical tension (West Asia) affecting crude/commodity prices and shipping; Regulatory delays (TREM5 design finalization); Customer concentration (exclusion of largest PV OEM); Inventory buildup (though days improved).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory spike to INR 75cr is purely scale-driven (days improved); TREM5 opportunity now niche (mufflers only for 19-37kW segment) but R&D spend aids export wins; Catalyst cost inflation masks true lightweighting volume growth in revenue % terms.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Scheme of arrangement] The journey timeline records a 2020 "Approval for Scheme of arrangements with NDR Auto Component Limited"; the deck gives no further detail on it.
- [Regulatory tailwinds] Growth strategy leans on BS 7 introduction (higher content per engine, market consolidation), CAFE III, China+1 supply-chain shifts, new emission norms in Europe and USA, and a customer-driven localisation push creating TA/JV opportunities for Indian partners.
- [Technology licensor scale] Donghee Industrial is described as a USD 2 billion revenue (CY2024) global player with 17 plants and 6 R&D centres across South Korea, Europe, China, USA and Mexico, and a strategic partner of 20+ global OEMs including Hyundai, Kia, VW and Stellantis.
- [Share capital change] Share capital rises from Rs 5.7 Cr at Mar-25 to Rs 11.5 Cr at Mar-26 in both standalone and consolidated balance sheets; the deck offers no explanation for the change.
- [Statement scope oddity] The standalone and consolidated P&L tables show identical revenue from operations (Q1 FY27 Rs 1,011.1 Cr; FY26 Rs 3,396.8 Cr) and identical EBITDA to a rounding difference (Rs 103.2 Cr consolidated vs Rs 103.3 Cr standalone in Q1 FY27), diverging only below EBIT via JV/associate share.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
